source.title: Provable Scaling Laws of Feature Emergence from Learning Dynamics of Grokking

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops a different theoretical account of grokking dynamics and reports experiments on group arithmetic, including modular addition, that bear on delayed generalization, feature emergence, and data-size boundaries.
record.gate_note: The paper also discusses results from other work, including numerical-stability explanations and ungrokking, but those cited results are not this study's results and are not recorded as rows. Figure-only outcomes are recorded as such; plotted values are not inferred.
record.test_reason: A theoretical account (Li² energy-function dynamics) with its own modular-addition and group-arithmetic experiments. It reports grokking with and without weight decay, test-accuracy phase boundaries against training-data ratio, learning-rate and initialization effects on generalization, and the learned features. These results bear directly on V1 and V5, and narrowly on V3 (initialization part) and V6 (across depth).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Additions: the authors present Li² (lazy, independent, then interactive feature learning) for 2-layer nets, extended to deeper ones. In their account, weight decay sets the strength of the feature-learning gradient and is sufficient but not necessary for grokking. Emergent features are local maxima of an energy E and are more efficient than memorization. A provable boundary n ≳ M log M separates generalization from memorization. Grokking's 'memorization' is overfitting random features, and Muon improves feature diversity.
record.recipe_differences: The study combines a theoretical energy-function analysis with experiments on two-layer and deeper group-arithmetic networks; it does not present itself as an explicit reproduction of either original source's experimental recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior varies with weight decay, learning rate, output-layer initialization, training-data fraction, network depth, and real versus complex weights.

fits_no_version.finding: Backpropagated-gradient norm |GF| and the cosine-distance weight updates show two stages (V updates, then W updates) before grokking. |GF| is larger with weight decay around epoch 100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking is preceded by a lazy phase in which the readout fits random features, followed by feature learning driven by the backpropagated gradient.

fits_no_version.finding: Muon achieves lower test loss than Adam when hidden width K is small relative to M (Figure 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Diversity-promoting optimizers improve generalization when width is limited on group arithmetic.

record.problems: The paper states that its local-maxima analysis relies on restrictive group-structure assumptions and that it does not analyze transition time between learning stages. Many plotted results have no numerical values or error bars in the text; several reported averages give seed counts but no uncertainty estimates. Some theory results depend on explicit assumptions about activation, representation, or initialization.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 6's separate weight-decay curves and Figure 10–11's full per-setting plots are represented only where retained rows capture the described outcome. Figure 12's ridge-readout comparisons, Figure 13's extended M=23 plot, and other training-fraction/init combinations in Figures 14–16 are omitted as additional or overlapping settings; the captions/text report the broad result that zero initialization accelerates feature learning, especially with scarce data. Figure 17's deeper-network initialization comparison and Figure 8's optimizer comparison are omitted. No cited findings are included as rows.

untested.parts: No quantitative delay-vs-training-set-size curve. The data-size trend is visible only from figure epoch ranges.
Gradual formation of the generalizing circuit, later removal of memorizing components, and progress measures anticipating the jump are all untested.
Non-algorithmic data (images, text, molecules) and full on/off switching by initialization scale or weight norm. Only top-layer zero-init on algorithmic data is tested.
Ungrokking below the critical size (only discussed via a citation).
Comparison across architectures other than MLP depth (e.g. transformers) or across hyperparameters beyond the learning-rate solution type.
All of it. Stable softmax and SGD are discussed only via cited work. Figure 8 compares Adam and Muon on final test loss, not on delay.

missing.what: Ridge-regression top layer: grokking still happens, slower for M=23 but faster for M=41/89/127 than baseline
Multi-layer zero-init speedup up to 10× (≈100 vs 1000 epochs)
Fig. 3 |GF| and ΔW two-stage dynamics with/without weight decay
Argument that grokking switches from overfitting on random features, not from memorization circuits, to generalization

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Most experimental outcomes are figure-only, with seed counts but no error bars. Several record values were corrected: R2/R3 sample count, R10 M, R22–R24 and R13 version links. The V6 link from R13 is narrow, resting on lowest-layer feature plots across depth.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests delayed generalization on algorithmic/group-arithmetic tasks and reports effects of training-data fraction and initialization on its timing. It does not establish a general quantitative law for delay versus training-set size across tasks.

The paper analyzes feature-learning dynamics and reports learned Fourier-like features. It does not track memorizing components being removed later or test whether continuous progress measures anticipate the accuracy jump.

The paper analyzes feature efficiency and a critical sample-size boundary, and compares weight decay conditions. It does not experimentally test an ungrokking transition below a critical dataset size.

rows.subject: two-layer nonlinear network (theoretical analysis)
rows.operation_detail: Derives the independent feature-learning dynamics as gradient ascent on an energy function and characterizes its local maxima
rows.measure: Feature-learning dynamics and feature solutions
rows.value: The independent dynamics exactly follows gradient ascent of E; its local maxima represent learned features, and for modular addition the local maxima are Fourier features.
rows.note: Theoretical result, not a reported numerical measurement of feature trajectories.
rows.check: Theorem-level derivation (energy function, local maxima are Fourier features), not a measurement. It does not show gradual circuit formation, later removal of memorization, or progress measures anticipating the jump, so it cannot bear on V2.
